subject: economics
objective: What is GDP by the expenditure approach?
instruction: The statistician of Riverside reports the following for the year. Household consumption was USD 45,000,000; firms' gross investment (including stock changes) was USD 12,500,000; the government spent USD 15,000,000. Riverside sold USD 8,200,000 of goods abroad and bought USD 9,700,000 from abroad. Because residents pay interest and profits to overseas owners, net factor income from abroad is minus USD 1,300,000. Capital consumption was USD 6,400,000. The population is 25,000 and the GDP deflator is 125. Use the expenditure method for GDP, gross national income (GNI) = GDP + net factor income from abroad, net national income (NNI) = GNI - depreciation, and real GDP = nominal GDP / GDP deflator x 100 (base year = 100). Per-person figures divide by the population. Required: gdp, net exports, gni, nni, real gdp, gdp per capita, real gdp per capita.
